text: The access-event code of a dashboard read is AGENT_MONITOR_READ and the code of a refusal is AGENT_MONITOR_DENY, both values of the access-event list in force and never constants in code; an entry carries the screen, the event code, the agent codes on screen, the business date or date range, the caller reference, the outcome and the time; the log read takes event, user, from, to, page and size with page bounds of the declared range; and the read index is on the event code, the caller reference and the business date. No metric value, agent output, prompt text or personal field is part of an entry. The entry is the record of a read that replaces the legacy lake copy: no lake table, no extract and no INT-19 or INT-20 path exists, and the entry of a read is what the access log answers back.
why: The legacy story names no field of an access entry and no event code, the TSD gives API-P4-008 the query members but no object set, and the FSD describes the event in prose only. DP-17 removes the lake copy that REQ-ACA-006 and NFR-042 name as the object of the logging rule, and the only record that can take its place is the access entry of the served read. The story still has to record what a reviewer needs to answer which analyst watched which agent and when, so the minimum set is fixed here and marked with the placeholder; the codes are list values, so a different code is a data change and not a code change.
read: Work Package B2-P4-027; context pack P4 (four provided operations, five tables, no event); TSD P4 v3 Appendix T-A.1 API-P4-008 and API-P4-012; FSD P4 v3 A2.4, A2.8 and AC-EXC-P4-001-05; legacy RWB-E1-063 sections 11, 15 and 17
applied_in: Sections 1, 3, 11, 12.1 and 12.7 of RWB-P4-E1063-APP; the ops_provided entry for the access-log read in the fragment
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-access with the owner of the access-log contract (RWB-P4-E1039-CON) at the wave 1 contract review
impact: If the list code or the field names differ, section 12.1, the entry of section 11 and the ops_provided string change; no criterion, no dependency and no table changes.

text: The dashboard opens on the Reporting read: the area is REPORTING from LOV-CAPABILITY, the right is R, and the letters are read from the permission rows of the version in force. RW-RISK and RW-COE hold R, RW-BIANAL holds CRUD and RW-CASEOWN holds none, as the legacy story states; every other role's Reporting letters are the matrix load's and are not restated here. A manual start of the daily rollup is guarded by Platform administration U, which RW-PLATADM holds through its CRUD letters. The metric read of rwb-agent keeps its own Rules and parameters R and the two rights are not merged.
why: The legacy story names Reporting R and the refusal of RW-CASEOWN, and TSD P4 T6.1 shows three of the 14 capability areas only, so the Reporting letters of the matrix are not stated for any role. The alternative right that this service's own table states is Rules and parameters R, which RW-CASEOWN holds, so using it would make the legacy refusal impossible; the legacy authority is therefore kept and the metric read's own right is left at its owner.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-063 sections 5, 7, 10 and 12; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and T6.2; FSD P4 v3 A2.4 (14 capability areas) and AC-EXC-P4-001-05; RWB-P10-E1063-CON section 12.1
applied_in: Sections 1, 5, 8, 10 and 12 of RWB-P4-E1063-APP; AC1, AC2 and AC6
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-access and rwb-agent owners at the wave 1 contract review
impact: If the Reporting area carries different letters, only the permission rows change and no criterion, path or table changes; if the right is moved to Rules and parameters, AC2 and TC-E1-063-08 have to be restated with a narrower right.

text: The access entry of a read is one entry of the service's local decision-record chain, appended through the platform library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the transaction window of the read and relayed by the outbox as rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1; the record code is taken from the library's code set at build time. No rwb.access.<Event>.v1 message is published by this slice and the two access event names of the service stay with the mapping, scope, delegation and reference-data stories.
why: FEAT-ACA-08 and FSD P4 A2.8 put the access log into the append-only decision log, and all other P4 stories of this run record an access entry the same way. DP-09 is the pattern the Work Package names for the outbox and CloudEvents envelope, and the ownership row of the service lists no event of its own, so the entry rides the shared topic instead of adding a third access event name.
read: Work Package B2-P4-027 (patterns DP09, DP15); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03, DP-09; context pack P4 (no event of this service, five tables, none an access table); FSD P4 v3 A2.8 and FEAT-ACA-08; legacy RWB-E1-063 section 17
applied_in: Sections 1, 4, 9, 12.3, 12.7 and 13 of RWB-P4-E1063-APP; events_published of the fragment
confirm: Ledger owner of the library RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and the rwb-decision owner at the wave 1 contract review
impact: If the library has no access record code, one code is added to its set (a library change, no schema change) and the story keeps one append per read; if a dedicated access event is preferred, events_published gains one name and section 12.3 changes only.

text: The access-event codes, the page bounds and the 2 s budget of the route are parameter rows read through the parameters contract of rwb-case, and the capability-area value REPORTING and the access-event list are reference rows read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case at the version in force. No code and no label is written in code, and the parameter and list codes are not specified in any source.
why: DP-06 and DP-07 are in the pattern set of this key and the FSD requires the capability areas and the letters as data. This service's own tables hold the letters per role but not the area catalogue or the list values, which stay with rwb-case, so the two reads are the only route that does not copy another service's data.

impact: If the area catalogue is served from another contract, section 12.2 and the lists fake change; the criteria and the entry shape do not.

text: The outbox and inbox library (DP-09), the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15) and the gateway-bff composite route contract (DP-19) are published and used from Day 1; their H rows are absent from the Work Package H list, which is copied unchanged, so the three are stated in sections 3 and 13 of the story instead of in the metadata row.
why: The DP table adds one build dependency per pattern and the Work Package fixes H as empty; the rows must be copied exactly, so the correction is carried in the story text and raised for the dependency map rather than written into the rows.

text: A read of the dashboard that cannot be recorded is not served: the route answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and no metric row reaches the screen. A partial read in which the metric answer times out is not recorded as a read of the screen.
why: The legacy story makes the copy the record and holds a publish that does not match; in the target the entry is the record, and a read that leaves no entry would be an unseen look at an agent's figures. No source states the failure rule for this screen, so the rule is stated here and marked.

applied_in: Sections 4 step 10, 5, 8 BR3 and 13 of RWB-P4-E1063-APP
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-access at the wave 1 contract review
impact: If the screen may be served unrecorded, BR3 and one exception row change, the ACs stay as they are and the fail-closed test case becomes a warning case.

text: A manual start of the daily rollup is an operation of rwb-agent (RWB-P10-E1063-APP); this story supplies the Platform administration U answer that guards it and the access entry of a refusal, and starts no workflow of its own. The legacy job admin read GET /admin/jobs and the rerun path under /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun are removed with the Quartz entry (DP-10).
why: The legacy story gives RW-PLATADM the rerun through the monolith job admin, and the target replaces Quartz with a Schedule whose rerun is a manual start of the same workflow identity. The right and the record are this service's; the start is the agent owner's, so the boundary is stated rather than a second operation invented.
